key_insight: Nonlinear nudging accelerates synchronization with the true Navier–Stokes flow by strengthening feedback as observation error decreases.
engineering_relevance: Finite element implementation supports flow-state reconstruction in complex geometries with physical boundary conditions, including from observations confined to a subregion.
method: Augment classical linear nudging with nonlinear error feedback.
Use an implicit–explicit finite element scheme with inf-sup stable elements.
Prove unconditional long-time stability and finite-time attainment of a prescribed error tolerance for the spatially semi-discrete scheme.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests in a periodic box, past a cylinder, and over a flat plate show considerably faster synchronization than linear nudging and demonstrate whole-flow synchronization from subregion observations.
watch_item: Observation resolution must be sufficiently fine for the nonlinear intensity and exponent; the analysis suggests χ = O(H⁻¹), and larger γ requires finer observations.
paper_title: Finite element nonlinear nudging for the Navier-Stokes equations
